headline: Govt introduces bill to replace RAB with Special Response Battalion
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act 2026 bill was introduced in Parliament to create a specialized unit under the police force.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' bill in the National Parliament on Thursday, proposing to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and replace it with the SRB.
caption:
RAB is set to be replaced by a new elite force called the Special Response Battalion (SRB).

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' bill in the National Parliament on Thursday, proposing to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and replace it with the SRB.

headline_marked: ACC [[seeks records from Asif Mahmud]] over corruption allegations
headline: ACC seeks records from Asif Mahmud over corruption allegations
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has requested appointment and promotion records from the Ministry of Youth and Sports to investigate claims of bribery and syndicates.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has written to the Ministry of Youth and Sports requesting four types of documents to investigate allegations of irregularities and corruption involving former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan and others.
The ACC has requested all appointment, promotion, and transfer records from Asif Mahmud's tenure, with a deadline of September 10 to submit the documents to the ACC headquarters.

Other officials under investigation include former Secretary of the Ministry of Youth and Sports Md. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Md. Masum Ahmed.
Allegations suggest a syndicate was formed to embezzle 7.6 million BDT by canceling the current duties of 38 Upazila Youth Development Officers and appointing them to new positions.

Further claims state that 15 million BDT was collected from 150 Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers in the name of promotions, and another 20 million BDT was exchanged for preferred postings.
The ACC has formed a four-member team led by Deputy Director Md. Zahid Kalam to investigate these claims of systemic bribery and tender-related corruption within the ministry.
caption:
ACC is investigating corruption allegations involving former adviser Asif Mahmud and top ministry officials.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has written to the Ministry of Youth and Sports requesting four types of documents to investigate allegations of irregularities and corruption involving former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan and others.

The ACC has requested all appointment, promotion, and transfer records from Asif Mahmud's tenure, with a deadline of September 10 to submit the documents to the ACC headquarters.

Other officials under investigation include former Secretary of the Ministry of Youth and Sports Md. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Md. Masum Ahmed.

Allegations suggest a syndicate was formed to embezzle 7.6 million BDT by canceling the current duties of 38 Upazila Youth Development Officers and appointing them to new positions.

Further claims state that 15 million BDT was collected from 150 Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers in the name of promotions, and another 20 million BDT was exchanged for preferred postings.

The ACC has formed a four-member team led by Deputy Director Md. Zahid Kalam to investigate these claims of systemic bribery and tender-related corruption within the ministry.

#Bangladesh #ACC #CorruptionInvestigation #AsifMahmud #Governance

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune
